claims.text: As-produced, pre-exposure Q235 steel contains microstructural inclusions such as MnS.
Pre-exposure Q235 steel has a heterogeneous native passive oxide film.
Localized corrosion in chloride-containing environments initiates primarily at MnS inclusions and grain-boundary defects in Q235 steel.
Inclusions and grain-boundary defects produce or sustain nonuniformity in the native passive oxide film.
Inclusion-associated regions undergo localized passive-film breakdown and consequently serve as pitting-initiation sites.
Elevated temperature accelerates chemical reactions and ion migration in the chloride environment.
The accelerated processes at elevated temperature further destabilize vulnerable passive-film regions and hasten pit nucleation and growth.
A heat treatment or purification process can reduce inclusion density in Q235 steel and promote a more uniform passive film.
Reducing inclusion prevalence will suppress the onset of localized corrosion in Q235 steel.
Inclusion-reduced Q235 steel will exhibit a lower pit density than untreated Q235 steel.
Inclusion-reduced Q235 steel with a more uniform passive film will exhibit a higher pitting potential than untreated Q235 steel.
Inclusion-reduced Q235 steel will exhibit a lower overall corrosion rate than untreated Q235 steel.
The corrosion-resistance improvement from inclusion reduction will be especially pronounced at elevated temperature.
Very high chloride concentrations may overwhelm the protective benefit of reducing inclusions.
Mechanical damage to the passive film may overwhelm the protective benefit of reducing inclusions.
The relative contributions of inclusions, bulk chemical composition, and stress to Q235 corrosion rates are not quantified here.
